one_liner: Collaborative work management platform with customizable CRM apps and workspaces

evidence.claim: Podio API uses OAuth2 with four documented flows (server-side, client-side, username/password, app authentication)
evidence.quote: The Podio API uses the OAuth2 protocol for authentication.

evidence.claim: API keys are self-serve from the account settings page after signing up for a Podio account
evidence.quote: You just have to sign in or sign up with Podio, and go to the API key tab in your settings.

evidence.claim: The API is free for both free and premium accounts with identical rate limits
evidence.quote: The Podio API is free to use for both premium and free Podio accounts. Both have full access to the API and have the same rate limits.

evidence.claim: REST API covers many object types including apps, items, workspaces, organizations, users, tasks, files, comments, webhooks
evidence.quote: REST API providing complete programmatic access to Podio apps, items, workspaces, organizations, users, tasks, files, comments, and webhooks.

evidence.claim: Podio provides an official MCP server over Streamable HTTP with OAuth 2.0 endpoints and dynamic client registration

notes: Official MCP server at mcp.podio.com supports three credential modes incl. dynamic client registration (RFC 7591). Classic REST API uses non-standard 'Authorization: OAuth2 ACCESS_TOKEN' header rather than Bearer; tokens expire after 8 hours (refresh tokens 28 days). App-authentication flow (app_id + app_token) suits headless/agent scripts. Programmatic access to app tokens requires contacting support. Podio is now owned by Progress/ShareFile; docs still hosted at developers.podio.com.
